CONTENT_MODELS_DESC: Govern Arclayer's official content protocols here, extend their continuation defaults, and preview impact before those changes reach the delivery plane.
CONTENT_MODELS_PROTOCOL_LIST_DESC: Each protocol keeps a locked system contract and a smaller extension layer.
CONTENT_MODELS_PROTOCOL_CANVAS_DESC: These locked nodes define routing, delivery, and publish semantics for every record created from this model.
CONTENT_MODELS_SYSTEM_NODE_ROUTING_DESC: Path ownership, dynamic matching, and public resolution rules stay system-managed here.
CONTENT_MODELS_SYSTEM_NODE_DELIVERY_DESC: The resolve payload, binding rules, and server-side flattening shape stay stable across workspaces.
CONTENT_MODELS_SYSTEM_NODE_WORKFLOW_DESC: Draft and published revisions stay isolated while the workflow keeps versioning and availability deterministic.
CONTENT_MODELS_EMPTY: No content types are available yet.
CONTENT_MODELS_FIELD_ROLE_HINT: Choose what kind of content this type most closely behaves like.
CONTENT_MODELS_FIELD_POSTURE_HINT: Decide whether new items should feel like pages, entries, compositions, or structured records.
CONTENT_MODELS_FIELD_SURFACE_HINT: Choose which editing surface opens first when someone continues this type.
CONTENT_MODELS_FIELD_STARTER_PACK_POLICY: Only use this when you need to fine-tune starting-content behavior beyond the standard content-type controls.
CONTENT_MODELS_STARTER_PACK_POLICY_INVAL: Starting content policy must be valid JSON.
CONTENT_MODELS_SECTION_CAPABILITIES_DESC: These capabilities explain what editors and workflows are available to items created from this type.
CONTENT_MODELS_GOVERNANCE_SYSTEM_DESC: These fields come from the official protocol contract and define the base structure and stable identifiers for the system object.
CONTENT_MODELS_GOVERNANCE_CUSTOM_DESC: These fields belong to the workspace extension layer and carry model-specific context on top of the official protocol.
CONTENT_MODELS_GOVERNANCE_WORKFLOW_DESC: This section shows how the model participates in draft, review, revision, and release-timing governance.
CONTENT_MODELS_GOVERNANCE_DELIVERY_DESC: This section gathers route, presentation, SEO, and surface contracts that keep the delivery plane stable.
CONTENT_MODELS_GOVERNANCE_GRAPHQL_DESC: This section exposes the model's current query-plane boundary for future schema builder and consumer work.
CONTENT_MODELS_SECTION_DEFAULTS_DESC: Adjust the model-owned defaults that are safe to extend without rewriting the system contract.
CONTENT_MODELS_SECTION_EXTENSIONS_DESC: Change how new items continue into work surfaces while the route and delivery contract stays locked.
CONTENT_MODELS_SECTION_ADVANCED_DESC: This section keeps low-level JSON policy out of the main flow. Use it only when the standard controls are not enough.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITIES_EMPTY: This content type does not expose any extra capabilities yet.
CONTENT_MODELS_EMPTY_BOUNDARY_CUSTOM: No custom fields exist yet. This protocol is still fully defined by the system contract.
CONTENT_MODELS_EMPTY_GOVERNANCE_WORKFLOW: No extra workflow capability is registered yet.
CONTENT_MODELS_EMPTY_GOVERNANCE_DELIVERY: No extra delivery capability is registered yet.
CONTENT_MODELS_EMPTY_GOVERNANCE_GRAPHQL: No extra GraphQL capability is registered yet.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_VERSIONED_DESC: Keep multiple draft and published revisions for the same content item.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_ROUTABLE_DESC: Give each item its own permalink that can be published on the site.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_TREEABLE_DESC: Organize items into nested structures such as page trees or navigable collections.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_VISUAL_EDITABL: Prepare this type for canvas-style layout editing when the visual builder is available.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_RICH_TEXT_EDIT: Open items in the writing editor for article-style drafting and editing.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_QUERYABLE_DESC: Treat items as structured records that can power lists, directories, and data-driven views.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_HAS_SLOTS_DESC: Allow editors to assemble content into reusable slot-based layouts.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_HAS_RELATIONS_: Link this type to other content so editors can model real relationships.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_LOCALIZABLE_DE: Manage translated or locale-specific versions of the same content item.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_PUBLISHABLE_DE: Draft, review, and publish items through the shared content workflow.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_SCHEDULABLE_DE: Plan future release timing instead of publishing items immediately.
CONTENT_MODELS_CAPABILITY_SEO_MANAGED_DE: Edit metadata such as title, description, and canonical settings from the content workbench.
CONTENT_MODELS_PREVIEW_BLOCKING: This preview would move content into recovery, so save is blocked.
CONTENT_MODELS_PREVIEW_READY: Preview is current. You can save these model defaults now.
CONTENT_MODELS_INSPECTOR_DESC: Preview the blast radius of extension changes before you commit them.
CONTENT_MODELS_INSPECTOR_EMPTY: Run an impact preview to see how this extension layer would affect existing content.
CONTENT_MODELS_CHANGE_PLAN_DIFF_EMPTY: This preview does not add any schema diff entries.
CONTENT_MODELS_PREVIEW_STALE: The draft changed after this preview. Run preview again to refresh the apply plan.
CONTENT_MODELS_UNSAVED_CHANGES: You have unsaved model changes. Discard them before switching protocols.
CONTENT_MODELS_APPLY_CONFIRM_DESC: This saves the next draft revision and keeps the current model workflow in sync.
CONTENT_MODELS_APPLY_CONFIRM_IMPACT: {{affected}} items are in scope. {{breaking}} breaking changes need review.
CONTENT_MODELS_SAVE_FAILED: Model defaults could not be saved.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DESC: Pages, articles, structured entries, and custom types all live here so you can preview, route, and continue the real work from one place.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_PERMALINK_DESC: Update the public address for this entry. Once saved, the library and follow-up publish flows will use the new permalink.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_PERMALINK_HELP: Enter only the path segment. You do not need to include a leading slash.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_VISIBILITY_DESC: Control whether this content is currently public or private.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_VISIBILITY_HELP: Public content can move into site and publish flows. Private content stays in the internal workbench.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_SEO_DESC: Add the key details that search and sharing surfaces will use.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_SEO_FIELD_TITLE_H: This is usually the first line people see in search results and browser tabs. Keep it clear and aligned with the page goal.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_SEO_FIELD_DESCRIP: This summary helps shape search-result snippets and share cards, so focus on the most important page context.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_SEO_FIELD_CANONIC: Only fill this in when this entry should point to one preferred public URL. Otherwise, leave it empty.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_PAGE_SETTINGS_DES: Keep this lightweight and only confirm the page basics that matter right now.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_STRUCTURED_FIELDS: Update the most important fields for this structured entry now, then continue with deeper data later.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_FIELD_TITLE_HELP: This is the primary name people use to recognize the entry across Content Library, preview, and follow-up editing flows.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_FIELD_SUMMARY_HEL: Use one or two short sentences to explain what this entry is so it stays legible in lists and previews.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DIALOG_FIELD_VISIBILITY_: Public content can move into site and publish flows. Private content stays in the internal workflow.
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_LOADING_DESC: Checking the backend continuation target for this content item.
CONTENT_PAGE_HANDOFF_TITLE: Page editing continues in Content Library for now
CONTENT_PAGE_HANDOFF_DESC: Until the real page editor exists, the primary page workflow stays in Content Library so you can keep working on permalink, SEO, and page settings there.
CONTENT_PAGE_HANDOFF_CARD_DESC: This page was created successfully. Return to the library preview and focused settings flows to continue working on it.
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED_TITLE: This content item needs recovery first
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_BLOCKED_DESC: The item exists, but continuation is currently blocked. Resolve the issue below before continuing.
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_SURFACE_UNAVAI: This content surface is not wired yet
The backend resolved this item to the {{surface}} surface, but Admin does not have a live continuation UI for it yet.
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_LOAD_ERROR_TIT: The continuation target could not be loaded
CONTENT_ITEM_CONTINUATION_LOAD_ERROR_DES: Admin could not load the backend continuation truth for this content item.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_DESC: Review the key details for this record here. When you need to keep editing fields, return to Content Library and continue through the real workbench flow.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_ITEM_DESC: This is a field-driven record. Confirm the basics first, then decide whether to continue editing the main fields.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_NEXT_DESC: Lightweight maintenance for structured content should still happen in Content Library. Return there to continue this record through the main-fields entry point.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_GUIDANCE_TITL: What this content type is best for
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_CONTEXT_DESC: Keep the essential context visible without turning this page into another abstract explanation shell.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_BOUNDARY_TITL: This record is not ready for deeper structured editing yet
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_BOUNDARY_DESC: The current content type is still missing part of the structured capability setup. Returning to Content Library is the most direct way to keep maintaining this record.
CONTENT_STRUCTURED_SURFACE_BOUNDARY_READ: This record already has the needed capabilities
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_DESC: Compose routed pages, global sections, and layout bindings from one focused builder surface.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_NAV_DESC: Move between routed pages, global sections, and reusable layout parts without leaving the builder surface.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_CANVAS_DESC: The active canvas item opens inside the builder shell and keeps its continuation context visible.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_CANVAS_BODY: Page composition, slot binding, and delivery-facing context all gather here so page work no longer detours back through Content Library.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_INSPECTOR_DESC: Keep section, layout, binding, and publish-facing controls close to the canvas.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_EMPTY_TITLE: Open a canvas item to start composing
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_EMPTY_DESC: Open any page or reusable section from Content Library to continue inside the builder.
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_BOUNDARY_TITLE: Canvas surface reached a capability boundary
CONTENT_SITE_BUILDER_BOUNDARY_DESC: The item resolved to canvas continuation, but its capability packs do not yet enable the visual builder workflow.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_CREATE_DIALOG_DESC: Pick one of the four official content protocols, then seed the draft before it enters Content Library.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DUPLICATE_DIALOG_DESC: Create a new draft copied from {{name}}.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_DELETE_DIALOG_DESC: Delete {{name}} and all of its versions. This action cannot be undone.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_UNARCHIVE_DIALOG_DESC: Restore {{name}} from archived back to draft.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_BULK_ARCHIVE_DIALOG_DESC: Archive the current content version of {{count}} selected items.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_BULK_DELETE_DIALOG_DESC: Delete {{count}} selected items and all of their versions. This action cannot be undone.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_PREVIEW_SUMMARY_EMPTY_ST: This structured entry does not have a summary yet.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_PREVIEW_STRUCTURED_NEXT_: Confirm the record basics here first, then continue editing the entry through field-level flows.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_EDITOR_SEO_DIALOG_DESC: Manage search metadata without leaving the article surface.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_VIEWS_MANAGER_DESC: Save and organize recurring workbench states without turning the library into a permanent rail.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_VIEWS_MANAGER_EMPTY: No saved views yet. Save the current workbench state to reuse it later.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_VIEW_CREATE_POPOVER_DESC: Preview the new view configuration before wiring it to shared persistence.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_VIEW_EDIT_DIALOG_DESC: Adjust the saved view metadata without changing the current workbench snapshot.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_VIEW_SAVE_AS_DIALOG_DESC: Duplicate this saved view with a new name, scope, and personal pin/default settings.

CONTENT_LIBRARY_EMPTY_FILTERED_DESC: Try another view, clear filters, or broaden your search.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_DESC: Choose a content type first, then create the draft.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_CREATE_DESC: Start by choosing what kind of content you want to create, then set the name, description, and a few type-specific details before the draft enters Content Library.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_SIDE_DESC: This flow creates the draft first, then lets you continue configuration later from Content Library.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRINCIPLE_ONE: A draft can be created before you decide every detail of the content structure.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRINCIPLE_TWO: The content type defines how work continues; the rest of the settings can come later.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRINCIPLE_THREE: You can return later and continue configuring the draft.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_STEP_ONE_DESC: Choose the content type first, then give the draft a name. You can continue the rest of the setup later from Content Library.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_STEP_ONE_SUPPORT: Continuing creates the draft record immediately. You do not need to finish every setting on this step.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_STEP_ONE_ASIDE_DESC: Creating the draft first lets the rest of the setup happen on a real content record.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_STEP_ONE_ASIDE_POINT_T: You can leave and continue later.
Additional setup can happen in a dedicated follow-up step.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_STEP_TWO_DESC: Add capabilities and other settings to the draft in the next step.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_TITLE_DESC: This name is used to identify the draft in Content Library after it is created.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_SUMMARY_DESC: Write a short description so people understand what this content is for before they open it.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_MODEL_DESC: Answer one question first: what kind of content are you creating? Official types cover common flows, and custom types live in the content types control center.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_MODEL_EMPTY: This workspace does not have any available content types yet. Create or adjust one in the content types control center, then come back to create content.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_MODEL_ERROR: Failed to load content types. Check the model configuration first.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_MODEL_CUSTOM_HIN: This is a custom type managed from the content types control center.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_TYPE_SETTINGS_EM: Choose a content type first. The next settings change based on what you are creating.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_ARTICLE_SETTINGS: Articles usually need a permanent link and publishing visibility before writing continues.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_PAGE_SETTINGS_DE: Pages benefit from a stable permanent link and a search snippet before layout work starts.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_REUSABLE_SECTION: Reusable sections need a stable section key so layouts and slots can reference them with confidence.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_CATEGORY_SETTING: Categories work best with a stable slug and visibility that keeps relation-driven views predictable.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_ROUTE_PATH_HELP: Use the public path this page should own. You can refine routing rules later from the page workbench.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_SECTION_KEY_HELP: This key is how layouts and slot bindings identify the reusable section across the site.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_CATEGORY_SLUG_HE: Keep this slug stable so page bindings and references can resolve the category consistently.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_PERMALINK_HELP: This becomes the permanent link for the draft. You can adjust it later from the content settings.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_ARTICLE_VISIBILI: Use public when the article should move through the normal publishing flow. Keep it private for internal drafts.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_PAGE_VISIBILITY_: Use public when the page should participate in delivery and preview flows. Keep it private while the route is still taking shape.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_REUSABLE_SECTION: Use private while a reusable section is still evolving. Switch to public when layouts should be able to rely on it.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_CATEGORY_VISIBIL: Use private for internal taxonomy work. Use public when pages and dynamic bindings should be able to consume the category.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_SEO_TITLE_HELP: This title appears in search results and browser tabs when the page is published.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_SEO_DESCRIPTION_: Keep this short and specific so the page makes sense outside the editor.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_START_FROM_DESC: Templates are now optional starting points. They no longer decide the content type or editor surface.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FIELD_LOCALE_DESC: Choose the locale you expect to work in first.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_FOOTER_READY_DESC: You can keep configuring it now or return from Content Library later.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_DRAFT_SUMMARY_DESC: This draft now exists in {{locale}} and is ready for further setup.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESETS_DESC: Templates are optional. Choose one if it helps you start faster.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_PAGE_DESC: Best for content that needs its own URL and page layout.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_PAGE_USE_CASE: this content should render as a page with URL, layout, and search metadata.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_POST_DESC: Best for articles, updates, and content published over time.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_POST_USE_CASE: this content belongs in a feed or collection and benefits from categorization.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_REUSABLE_BLOCK_: Best for shared content reused across multiple pages.
the same content needs to stay portable and reusable.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_EMAIL_TEMPLATE_: Best for reusable email content and localized campaigns.
this content is intended for email delivery rather than page rendering.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_TAXONOMY_ITEM_D: Best for categories, tags, and other content used for organization.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_TAXONOMY_ITEM_U: this content is primarily used to classify or organize other content.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_BLANK_DESC: Start with a draft that does not include any predefined capabilities.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PRESET_BLANK_USE_CASE: you want to start from scratch and decide the structure later.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_CAPABILITY_PACKS_DESC: Choose the behaviors this content should support.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_ROUTABLE_DESC: Give the content a public URL or path.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_PUBLISHABLE_DESC: Allow the content to move through draft and published states.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_SEO_DESC: Store search metadata alongside the content.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_LAYOUT_BOUND_DESC: Associate the content with a page layout or composition context.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_REUSABLE_DESC: Allow the content to be inserted or referenced in multiple places.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_TAXONOMY_DESC: Use the content to organize or classify other content.
CONTENT_BOOTSTRAP_PACK_SCHEDULABLE_DESC: Support scheduled publishing or timed state changes.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_ROW_SUMMARY_EMPTY_ARTICL: This article does not have a description yet.
CONTENT_LIBRARY_ROW_SUMMARY_EMPTY_PAGE: This page does not have a description yet.
CONTENT_TYPE_ARTICLE_DESC: Best for news, blog posts, journals, and other content that is primarily read as a long-form entry.
CONTENT_TYPE_PAGE_DESC: Best for website pages, landing pages, campaigns, and other content that needs a stable address.
CONTENT_TYPE_REUSABLE_SECTION_DESC: Best for headers, footers, and shared layout building blocks that should stay reusable across pages.
CONTENT_TYPE_CATEGORY_DESC: Best for relation-first taxonomy records that organize articles, pages, and other structured content.
